title: The Salty water of the bay
subtitle: 江河湖海 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 江河湖海（自然生态·海洋与河流）
meta: 主题语境：江河湖海（自然生态·海洋与河流）　|　核心词汇：salty　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 salty 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1981 the trader wrote of ① a salty water of the bay in the list, and everybody in the market said at once that it was ② saltier than the one named there the year before. Three weeks on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the trader, who never explained anything, had done it twice over and gone home; it was the salty ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the saltiest water of the bay anybody in the market had ever seen, or so the list for October 1975 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too salty to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the partner who had come to help; the salty ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the basket at the far stall, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a salty wind from the sea, and said that no partner in his right mind would call it ⑥ as salty as the wind from the sea they had once had in the old market. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was salty or not, and he said so.

By 1988 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the list. What the line asked for was ⑦ something salty, and nothing besides. The partner from the next market called the whole plan ⑧ quite salty; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the list kept the names of the salty ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1991, year after year, she wrote of another salty water of the bay in the same list, and the work, which took two weeks, seemed ⑨ saltier than anybody had expected. ⑩ The saltiest wind from the sea in the whole market, she said in 1993, was the one she could never quite name; the salty ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 咸（前置定语 a salty water of the bay：1981 年货商在货单里记下的那件咸的水）
B. adj. 咸／带咸味（比较级 saltier than：文中两处，一处比海湾里咸涩的水，一处比预想）
C. adj. 咸／带咸味（最高级 the saltiest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 咸（表语 too salty to do：母亲觉得它太咸，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 带咸味（前置定语 a salty wind from the sea：叔叔把整件事称作一桩带咸味的风）
F. adj. 带咸味（同级比较 as salty as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩海上带咸味的风相比）
G. adj. 带咸味（后置定语 something salty：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 带咸味（受程度副词修饰 quite salty：那位伙计的评价）

items.q: a salty water of the bay
the saltiest water of the bay anybody
a salty wind from the sea
The saltiest wind from the sea in

answers.why: salty 意为“咸”，1981 年货商在货单里记下的是“一件咸的水”，此处作前置定语 a salty water of the bay。
salty 意为“咸”，此处用比较级 saltier than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
salty 意为“咸”，货单上 十月 那行字说它是集市里最咸的一件，故用最高级 the saltiest water of the bay。
salty 意为“咸”，母亲认为这件东西“太咸了，谁也用不上”，too salty to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
salty 意为“带咸味”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩带咸味的风”，此处作前置定语 a salty wind from the sea。
salty 意为“带咸味”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩海上带咸味的风一样带咸味”，同级比较用 as salty as。
salty 意为“带咸味”，货单上那半行字要的是“带咸味的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something salty。
salty 意为“带咸味”，邻集市来的那位伙计认为这套计划“相当带咸味”，quite 修饰原级 salty。
salty 意为“带咸味”，1991 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要带咸味”，故用比较级 saltier than。
salty 意为“带咸味”，母亲 1993 年说的是“整个集市里最带咸味的那一桩”，故用最高级 the saltiest wind from the sea。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1981 年，货商在货单里记下了一件咸的水。（a salty water of the bay）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更咸。（saltier than …）
母亲觉得它太咸，谁也用不上。（too salty to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩带咸味的风。（a salty wind from the sea）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩海上带咸味的风一样带咸味。（as salty as …）
到了 1988 年，货单上只剩半行字：要的是一件带咸味的东西。（something salty）
answers: In 1981 the trader wrote of a salty water of the bay in the list.
Everybody said it was saltier than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too salty to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a salty wind from the sea.
He said nobody would call it as salty as the wind from the sea they had once had.
By 1988 the list asked for nothing but something salty.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 salty 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1981 the trader wrote of a salty water of the bay in the list, and nobody forgot it.
It was the saltiest water of the bay in the market, or so the list says.
My mother thought it too salty to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a salty wind from the sea, and nobody argued with him.
The partner from the next market called the plan quite salty, and everybody laughed.
The salty ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
